header: The documents the card's page links open in its own viewer (pure): a page number on the card opens that page of the document, drawn with the quoted words marked (DocViewer.tsx, PdfPageView.tsx). I keep every one of them ONCE in Vercel Blob (scripts/upload-history-docs.ts) and serve it by our own route, GET /api/history-docs/<id> (serve.ts), because the browser cannot read another site's PDF itself (pdf.js needs the bytes), the browser's own viewer cannot mark words, and fetching a publisher's file live from our server is not dependable (sail.co.in serves an incomplete certificate chain that Node refuses; a ministry's site may refuse a data centre).
* INTERNAL documents (the two JO Manuals 2022, which have no web address): the reader must be signed in.

* PUBLISHED PDFs (SAIL's Steel Cities book, the annual reports, the Lok Sabha replies, an obituary): public, so anyone may read them; their own address (`remote`) is where the copy came from and where "Open the whole document" leads. I serve only the ids below: the route is not a general proxy.
The page numbers the card cites are checked against the text of each PDF (scripts/check-manual-marks.ts: every cited quote is found on its page).

members.name: title
doc: This is the name the reader sees at the top of the viewer.

members.name: blobName
doc: I save the copy under this name in Blob (the upload adds a random suffix).

members.name: file
doc: For an internal document: its file as received (the upload reads it from a folder) and its number of pages.

members.name: remote
doc: For a published PDF: its own address (the upload downloads it from there; "Open the whole document" leads there).
